exercises.name: Seated Reaching for Cones
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin sitting upright with a partner standing in front of you. Your partner should be holding a cone or other small object.
Movement
  • As your partner holds the cone in front of you, reach with one arm and try to touch the cone, then repeat. Your partner should change the position of the cone to challenge your reach.
Tip
  • Challenge yourself to reach cones that require shifting your weight. Make sure to keep your balance as you reach.

exercises.name: Side to Side Weight Shift with Overhead Reach and Counter Support
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in a standing upright position with your feet shoulder width apart and your hands resting on a counter.
Movement
  • Shift your weight to one side as you reach your same side arm overhead. Repeat to the opposite side.
Tip
  • Make sure to maintain an upright posture and use the counter to help you balance as needed.

exercises.name: Supine Hip Extension with Footstool (AKA)
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin lying on your back with a footstool underneath the end of your residual limb.
Movement
  • Lift your hip up off the table, pushing your residual limb against the footstool. Hold briefly, then lower back down and repeat.
Tip
  • Try not to use your sound leg to perform the bridge. Make sure to keep your core engaged and do not arch your back.

exercises.name: Lateral Step Over with Beam (AKA)
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in a standing upright position to the side of a beam on the floor.
Movement
  • Step sideways over the beam with the foot closest to the beam, leaving enough room for your second foot to step, and follow with your other foot. Return to the other side in the same manner and and continue down the beam.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your movements controlled and maintain your balance during the exercise.

exercises.name: Standing with Feet Together on Foam Pad (BKA)
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in a standing upright position with a foam pad on the ground in front of you.
Movement
  • Place your feet together on the foam pad and maintain your balance in this position.
Tip
  • Make sure to maintain good posture, keep your core engaged, and evenly distribute your weight on both legs during the exercise.

exercises.name: Forward and Backward Step Over with Beam (BKA)
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in a standing upright position with a beam on the floor in front of you.
Movement
  • Step forward over the beam with one foot and follow with your other foot. Reverse the action and repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure to maintain your balance and look down at the beam as needed during the exercise. Focus on shifting your weight onto the prosthetic limb before stepping.

exercises.name: Forward Monster Walk
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in a wide stance position in shallow water with web gloves on your hands.
Movement
  • Take a large step forward, circling your foot inward then out to your side, at the same time mirror the movement with your opposite hand. Repeat with your other arm and leg.
Tip
  • Make sure to maintain your balance and an upright posture during the exercise. Focus on fast outward motion of your opposing hand and leg. Modification: If you are unable to coordinate your hand and leg movements, keep your arms still and only move your legs. Progression: As you gain control increase your speed with the outward motion of your arms and legs.

exercises.name: Deep Water Jogging
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in an upright position wearing a lumbar float belt and web gloves.
Movement
  • Bend one knee up while your opposite leg extends and pushes backwards, your arms will move opposite your legs and scoop water backwards.
Tip
  • Lean slightly forward when jogging and focus on the fast backward movement of your arm and legs. Make your movements smooth and controlled during the exercise.Modification: You can remove the web gloves and make fists with your hands to focus mainly on leg propulsion.Progression: As you gain more control, increase your speed with the movement.

exercises.name: Sit to Stand
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin sitting upright with your feet flat on the ground underneath your knees.
Movement
  • Move your shoulders and head over your toes, bring your knees forward, and allow your hips to come off the chair, then push down equally into both feet to stand up. Sit back down and repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your weight evenly distributed between both legs, and try to keep your back straight throughout the exercise. Do not lock out your knees once you are standing.

exercises.name: Forward Step Up
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in a standing upright position, with a step in front of you, holding onto a stable surface for support.
Movement
  • Step forward onto the step with one foot, then step up with your other foot. Step back down to the ground in the reverse order.
Tip
  • Try to make sure to start the movement by bending your knee first then lifting your foot up to the step. Maintain your balance during the exercise.

exercises.name: Recumbent Bike
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin by sitting on the bike seat and check that it is in the correct position. To adjust the seat, look for a lever to the side or below the seat. You should be able to reach the pedal at its farthest point with a slight bend in your knee.
Movement
  • You may need to press a "Start" or "Quick Start" button to start the session. Start pedaling your legs, pressing your feet forward and down on the pedals in a circular motion. Continue to bike for the instructed amount of time.
Tip
  • Make sure to stay seated upright and keep your movements fluid and controlled.You can increase your resistance using the up and down arrows on the control panel to make your workout more challenging.When you are done with your workout, stop pedaling, and carefully get off of the bike.

exercises.name: Elliptical
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin by holding onto the stationary handles and step up onto the machine one foot at a time, first on the lower pedal, then onto the other pedal. You may need to press a "Start" or "Quick Start" button to start the session.
Movement
  • Jog forward, pressing down on the pedals with each foot. You can either hold onto the stationary handles for balance or the moving handles for an increased workout. Continue to jog for the instructed amount of time.
Tip
  • Make sure to maintain an upright posture and keep your movements fluid and controlled.To adjust your resistance and incline, look for either toggles or buttons with arrows on the control panel. Press the arrows up to increase your resistance or incline. To change these controls quickly, you can hold the controls down until you reach your desired resistance or incline.When you are done with your workout, slow down and stop pedaling, then carefully step off of the machine, leading with the foot that is higher.

exercises.name: Tip Pinch with Putty
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin sitting upright with a roll of putty on the table.
Movement
  • Using the tips of your index finger and thumb, gently pinch into the putty.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your wrist straight and only move through a pain free range.

exercises.name: Seated Gripping Towel
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin sitting upright with your arm resting on a table, hand off the edge, holding a rolled towel.
Movement
  • Squeeze the towel, then relax and repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep the rest of your arm relaxed during the exercise.

exercises.name: Wrist AROM Wrist Circumduction
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Start with your elbow on the table and your hand in a loose fist. Hold onto your arm below your wrist with your other hand to keep it still.
Movement
  • Imagine a butterfly landing on your hand. Make small circles with your fist to give the butterfly a fun ride. Then pause, and switch directions.
Tip
  • Be sure to keep your arm still. Focus on only moving at your wrist.

exercises.name: Hand AROM Tendon Glides
exercises.description:
Setup

  • Start with your elbow on the table. Your wrist should be straight and your fingers relaxed.

Movement

  • Flatten your fingers as if you were going to make a hand puppet. Then, curl your fingers so your finger tips touch the top of your palm, the bottom of your palm, and the middle of your palm. Straighten all of your fingers as if you were going to give a highfive, and repeat.

Tip

  • Keep your movements smooth and slow. Try to keep your wrist straight the whole time.

exercises.name: Lower Cheek Self Massage
exercises.description:
Setup

  • Begin with your face relaxed.

Movement

  • Place your thumb on the inside of your mouth and your index finger on the outer cheek of your affected side. Gently squeeze your index finger and thumb as you pull your cheek towards your lips. Repeat by moving your fingers to a different starting positioning on the same cheek. Switch your hands and repeat on the other cheek.

Tip

  • Apply a warm cloth to your upper lip for 5-10 minutes before the exercise. It may be helpful to perform this exercise in front of a mirror to check the accuracy of your movement. 

Muscle

  • Buccinator and Risorius

exercises.name: Pucker Lips
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin with your face relaxed
Movement
  • Press your lips together and pucker your lips as if you are giving a kiss. Hold for 10-20 seconds, relax and repeat.
Tip
  • Try not to over exaggerate and focus on moving both sides of your face symmetrically. Do not let your unaffected side lead the movement. Perform this exercise in front of a mirror to check for accuracy. Modification: If you are having difficulty controlling the movement or see unwanted movement, relax your face to a point where you have control. Hold this position for a few seconds, then try the full movement again. Focus on watching and feeling what your unaffected side is doing and try to visualize doing the same movement on your affected side. Muscle: Orbicularis Oris

exercises.name: Closing Eyes
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin with your face relaxed.
Movement
  • Close your eyes gently, then tightly. Hold for 10-20 seconds, relax and repeat.
Tip
  • Try not to over-exaggerate the movement. Focus on closing both eyes equally. When your eyes are closed tightly, the skin around your forehead, temples, and cheeks will be drawn towards your eyes. It may be helpful to perform this exercise in front of a mirror to check the accuracy of your movement. Modification: If you are having difficulty controlling the movement, relax your face to a point where you have control. Hold this position for a few seconds, then try the full movement again. Focus on feeling what your unaffected side is doing and try to do the same movement on your affected side. Muscle: Orbicularis Oculi

exercises.name: Prone on Elbows Stretch
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin lying on your front with your hands by your head.
Movement
  • Push yourself up onto your elbows with your head facing forward. Hold this position.
Tip
  • Make sure to maintain a gentle chin tuck during the exercise.

exercises.name: Standing Lumbar Spine Flexion Stretch Counter
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in a standing upright position with your hands resting on a table.
Movement
  • Slowly walk backward, bending at your hips and keeping your hands on the table, until you feel a stretch in your back.
Tip
  • Make sure to only move in a pain-free range of motion during the exercise.

exercises.name: Seated Trunk Rotation
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin sitting upright with your feet on the floor and your arms crossed and held up in front of your body.
Movement
  • Turn your head and shoulders as far as you can to one side, then turn all the way back to your opposite side, and repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your shoulders relaxed and down during the exercise. Move your head and shoulders as one unit and maintain your balance as you turn.

exercises.name: Supine Cross Body Shoulder Stretch
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin lying on your back.
Movement
  • Lift one arm across your body, then gently press on your elbow with your opposite arm until you feel a stretch in your shoulder and hold.
Tip
  • Make sure to only move through a pain free range of motion and continue breathing evenly during the stretch.

exercises.name: Seated Bilateral Shoulder External Rotation with Resistance
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin sitting upright with your elbows bent and a towel roll tucked under each arm, holding the ends of a resistance band in each hand.
Movement
  • Slowly rotate your arms outward, pulling the resistance band. Hold, then slowly bring your hands back to the starting position and repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure to squeeze your shoulder blades together and down. Keep your neck and back straight and do not shrug your shoulders during the exercise.

exercises.name: Supine Hamstring Stretch
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin lying on your back with one leg bent and your other leg straight.
Movement
  • Lift your straight leg up toward the ceiling and pull it towards yourself with your hands, feeling a stretch in the back of your leg. Hold this position.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your leg straight and back flat on the bed during the exercise.

exercises.name: Quadruped Weight-Bearing Activity: Reaching
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin on your hands and knees toward the end of a table or mat, so that your feet are near or off the edge. Align your hands directly under your shoulders.
Movement
  • Lift your non-affected arm forward at shoulder-height level. Hold this position for 3-4 seconds.Then, bring your arm back down to the starting position. Relax and repeat.
Tip
  • Do not do this activity if you feel light-headed or dizzy. Do not hang on your affected shoulder. Keep your shoulder strong and level with your back. Engage your core muscles.

exercises.name: Seated UE Activity: Weight-Bearing Side-To-Side Shifts
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin sitting upright at the edge of a chair or bed with your feet flat on the floor. Hold onto the edge of the surface you're sitting on with both hands. You may need someone to assist you throughout the exercise.
Movement
  • Lean toward one side and shift your weight onto one hand. Hold this position for 3-4 seconds. Then, repeat on the opposite side. Continue alternating leaning and shifting your weight through each hand.
Tip
  • Make sure to push through your hands and not through your feet throughout the exercise. Keep your shoulders relaxed throughout the activity.

exercises.name: Seated Balance Activity: Lateral Reaching
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin sitting upright at the edge of a bed or chair with your feet flat on the floor. You may need someone to assist you throughout the exercise.
Movement
  • With your non-affected arm, reach out to the side at shoulder level as far as possible. Turn your head to look at your arm. Return to the center. Then, reach the same arm across your body toward the opposite side as far as possible, twisting your trunk and turning your head to look at your arm. Relax and repeat.
Tip
  • Do not do this activity if you feel light-headed or dizzy. Make sure your affected arm is in a safe position throughout the exercise to avoid injury. Do not lift your hips up as you are reaching.

exercises.name: Standing Cervical Flexion AROM
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in a standing upright position.
Movement
  • Bend your head forward, tucking your chin towards your chest, then return to the starting position and repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your back straight and do not let your head bend or rotate to either side.

exercises.name: Standing Cervical Sidebending AROM
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in a standing upright position.
Movement
  • Tilt your head sideways, pulling your ear toward one shoulder, then return to the starting position and repeat toward the other side.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your back straight and do not let your head rotate, move forward or move backward.

exercises.name: Seated Wrist Extension with Dumbbell
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Sit with one arm resting on a table, grasping a lightweight dumbbell and palm facing downward.
Movement
  • Bend your wrist backwards towards your body, then slowly return to the starting position.
Tip
  • Make sure to only move your wrist, and avoid any forearm or shoulder movement during the exercise.

exercises.name: Seated Wrist Flexion with Dumbbell
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Sit with one arm resting on a table, grasping a lightweight dumbbell and palm facing upward.
Movement
  • Curl your wrist towards your body, then slowly return to the starting position.
Tip
  • Make sure to only move your wrist, and avoid any forearm or shoulder movement during the exercise.

exercises.name: Seated Toe Raise
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin sitting upright on a chair with your feet flat on the floor.
Movement
  • Raise your toes up off the floor.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your heels on the floor.

exercises.name: Toe Spreading
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in a standing upright position with your feet shoulder width apart, looking down at your feet.
Movement
  • Gently spread your toes apart to cause the arch of your foot to rise away from the ground.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your foot in contact with the ground.

exercises.name: Seated Finger DIP PROM
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin by gently pinching the end of your finger at the last knuckle.
Movement
  • Slowly bend the end of your finger using your other hand.
Tip
  • Make sure to only move through a pain-free range of motion.

exercises.name: Seated Finger Composite Flexion Extension
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin this exercise with your wrist and fingers straight.
Movement
  • Slowly bend the top two knuckles of your fingers downward. Pause, then return to the starting position and repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure to only move through a pain-free range of motion. Try to keep your wrist straight as you move your fingers.

exercises.name: Lateral Lunge
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in a standing upright position with your feet shoulder width apart and arms resting at your side.
Movement
  • Step to the side with one leg, lowering your body into a lunge position, then carefully return to the starting position.
Tip
  • Make sure not to let your knees collapse inward during the exercise.

exercises.name: Forward T
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in a standing upright position with your hands resting at your waist.
Movement
  • Balancing on one leg, bend at your hips and slowly tilt your body forward while extending the other leg backward, then return to the starting position and repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your back straight, and don't let your knee collapse inward during the exercise.

exercises.name: Prone Knee Flexion AROM
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin lying face down with your legs laying flat.
Movement
  • Bend one knee, bringing your foot as close as possible toward your body. Once a stretch is felt, hold the position.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your upper body relaxed during the exercise and do not arch your back as you bend your knee.

exercises.name: Long Sitting Quad Set
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin sitting upright on the floor with one leg laying straight and your other knee bent.
Movement
  • Straighten your leg, pushing your knee toward the floor, and hold.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your back straight during the exercise.

exercises.name: Supine Pelvic Tilt
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin lying on your back with your knees bent and hands resting on the bottom of your ribs.
Movement
  • Slowly tilt your pelvis backwards, trying to draw your navel towards your spine and flatten your spine to the ground. Reverse the motion by tilting your pelvis forward. Repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your movements slow and controlled and try to keep your stomach still.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin on all fours, with your arms positioned directly under your shoulders.
Movement
  • Straighten one arm and your opposite leg at the same time, until they are parallel to the floor. Hold briefly, then return to the starting position.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your abdominals tight and hips level during the exercise.

exercises.name: Pelvic Tilt on Swiss Ball
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin sitting upright on a swiss ball, holding onto a chair at your side.
Movement
  • Keeping your shoulders and upper body still, roll the ball backward and forward by moving just your pelvis.
Tip
  • Make sure to maintain your balance and do not to let your upper back slump during the exercise.

exercises.name: Pelvic Circles on Swiss Ball
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin sitting upright on a swiss ball with your feet resting on the ground hip width apart, holding onto a chair at your side.
Movement
  • Slowly rotate your hips in a circle, first clockwise, then counterclockwise.
Tip
  • Make sure to maintain your balance and good posture during the exercise. Try to only move your hips.

exercises.name: Shoulder PNF D2 with Resistance
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin standing upright with one arm crossed in front of your body, thumb pointing down, holding a resistance band that is looped around the opposite foot.
Movement
  • Diagonally raise your arm overhead across your body, turning your arm so your thumb points up. Slowly reverse the movement and repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your elbow straight. Do not shrug your shoulders or arch your low back during the exercise.

exercises.name: Scaption with Dumbbells
exercises.description:
Setup

  • Begin in a standing upright position with your arms resting at your side, grasping lightweight dumbbells

Movement

  • Slowly raise your arms diagonally at roughly a 30 degree angle from your body, then lower your arms back to your sides.

Tip

  • Make sure to keep your elbows straight and avoid shrugging your shoulders. Try not to arch your low back while raising and lowering your arms.

exercises.name: Seated Trunk Rotation - Arms Crossed
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin sitting upright in a chair with your arms crossed over your chest.
Movement
  • Slowly rotate your trunk to one side, then return and repeat the rotation on your other side.
Tip
  • Make sure to stay upright throughout the exercise and do not bend forward or backward.

exercises.name: Cat Cow
exercises.description:
Setup

  • Begin on all fours with your arms directly under your shoulders and knees bent 90 degrees.

Movement

  • Slowly round your back up toward the ceiling, then let it sag down to the floor while looking up, and repeat.

Tip

  • Make sure to use your entire back for the motion and keep your movements slow and controlled.

exercises.name: Isometric Jaw Abduction
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in an upright sitting position.
Movement
  • Place your fist under your chin and apply a gentle pressure as you try to open your jaw slightly.
Tip
  • Make sure not to let your jaw shift to either side during the exercise.

exercises.name: Standing Isometric Cervical Flexion with Manual Resistance
exercises.description:
Set Up
  • Begin in a standing upright position with your feet shoulder width apart.
Movement
  • Gently tuck your chin. Place your hand on your forehead head and apply pressure, using your neck muscles to keep your head steady.
Tip
  • Do not let your head tilt or rotate during the exercise.

exercises.name: Hip Flexor Stretch with Noodle
exercises.description:
Setup

  • Begin standing tall, holding onto the pool wall in front of you with one leg straight behind you, resting on a noodle. Your parent can help you get your leg onto the noodle if needed.

Movement

  • Keep your leg relaxed and let the noodle hold your leg up so you feel a light stretch in the front of your hip. Hold this position, then relax and repeat.

Tip

  • Make sure that the noodle is not too big for you to control the stretch. If your muscles are tighter, stand in shallower water.

exercises.name: Hamstring Stretch with Noodle
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin standing tall, holding onto the pool wall at your side with your outside leg raised straight in front of you and resting on a pool noodle.
Movement
  • Keep your leg relaxed and let the noodle hold your leg up so you feel a light stretch in the back of your leg. Hold this position, then relax and repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure that the noodle is not too big for you to control the stretch. If your muscles are tighter, stand in shallower water.

exercises.name: Warrior II
exercises.description:
Setup

  • Begin standing tall with your feet wide apart and tummy pulled in.

Movement

  • Stretch your arms out to your sides as you turn one foot out. Imagine you are a strong warrior as you lunge to the side and look out over your fingertips.

Tip

  • Remember to breathe in and out during the exercise.

exercises.name: Cat Cow
exercises.description:
Setup

  • Begin on all fours.

Movement

  • Keep your back straight and shoulders down and remember to breathe during the exercise.

Tip

  • Remember to breathe during the exercise. If you'd like, try making cat and cow noises throughout the exercise.

exercises.name: Army Crawl
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Position your child lying face down and propped up on their forearms.
Movement
  • Help your child shift their weight side to side by moving their opposite arm and legs forward one at a time.
Tip
  • Alternate your hand placement to each shoulder and hip to assist with their crawling motion.
  • Play: Place toys 1-2 feet in front of your child to encourage forward crawling.

exercises.name: Prone to All Fours
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Position your child lying face down.Use your hands to assist your child under their shoulders and chest so they use their arms to push up onto all fours.
Movement
  • Keep your child's legs from crossing behind them and maintain light pressure over their hips down to the floor.
Tip
  • Play: Place a toy in front of your child to draw their attention forward. This may help facilitate your child moving themselves into the hands-knees position.

exercises.name: Wrist AROM Wrist Circumduction
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Start with your elbow on the table and your hand in a loose fist. Hold onto your arm below your wrist with your other hand to keep it still.
Movement
  • Imagine a butterfly landing on your hand. Make small circles with your fist to give the butterfly a fun ride. Then pause, and switch directions.
Tip
  • Be sure to keep your arm still. Focus on only moving at your wrist.

exercises.name: Hand AROM Tendon Glides
exercises.description:
Setup

  • Start with your elbow on the table. Your wrist should be straight and your fingers relaxed.

Movement

  • Flatten your fingers as if you were going to make a hand puppet. Then, curl your fingers so your finger tips touch the top of your palm, the bottom of your palm, and the middle of your palm. Straighten all of your fingers as if you were going to give a highfive, and repeat.

Tip

  • Keep your movements smooth and slow. Try to keep your wrist straight the whole time.

exercises.name: Walking Uphill
exercises.description:
Setup

  • Begin standing at the bottom of a hill or on a treadmill set at an incline to walk up.

Movement

  • Keep your toes facing forward, focusing on placing your heel on the ground first as you walk up the hill or incline.

Tip

  • Start slow until you feel comfortable with the walking pattern, then increase your speed or time and distance to make it more challenging. Your caregiver should be with you at all times if you are using a treadmill.

exercises.name: Walking Backwards
exercises.description:
Setup

  • Begin standing tall at the start of a long hallway, open space, or treadmill

Movement

  • Step backwards, making sure your heel hits the ground with each step.

Tip

  • Be sure to move any obstacles in your path out of the way before walking and have a partner closeby for safety. Your caregiver should be with you at all times if you are using a treadmill.

exercises.name: Prone over Leg
exercises.description:
Setup

  • Sit with your legs extended on the floor, on a blanket or mat for comfort. Baby should be happy and comfortable, unswaddled in your arms.

Movement

  • Gently place baby on their tummy over your thigh, elbows propped on top of your thigh or extended towards the floor over your thigh. Keep hands supporting arms or shoulders and trunk if needed, and encourage baby to lift head up to look around.

Tip

  • Place a mirror in front of baby for visual motivation to look up and lift head.

exercises.name: Non-Nutritive Oral Skills with Baby's Hand
exercises.description:
Setup

  • Hold baby comfortably in your arms, either facing you straight on, or in a cradle hold.Start by gently holding baby's hand with your finger.

Movement

  • Start by gently guiding baby's own fingers to their mouth. Help baby move their hand back and forth over lips and mouth and pause with hand to mouth to allow baby to explore their hand with the tongue and mouth as tolerated.

Tip

  • Smile, coo, and engage with baby. Move slowly and read baby's cues for stress, including furrowed brow, pursed lips, grimacing, moving head away, crying, or gagging.

exercises.name: Quad Set
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin sitting on the ground or a bed with one leg straight and your opposite leg bent.
Movement
  • Squeeze the muscles in the top of your thigh, gently pressing your knee down toward the bed. Hold, then relax and repeat.
Tip
  • Sit tall during the movement and keep your knee straight. Focus on squeezing the thigh muscles closer to your knee.

exercises.name: Single Knee to Chest Stretch
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin lying on your back with your legs straight.
Movement
  • Slowly lift one leg and hug your knee toward your chest until you feel a gentle stretch in your low back and hold.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep you back relaxed and your opposite leg flat on the surface.

exercises.name: Supine Caregiver Abdominal Wall 'ILU' Massage
exercises.description:
Setup
  • The child should be lying on their back on a bed or the floor.
Movement
  • The caregiver should first apply a gentle 'I' stroke from the top of the belly to the bottom of the belly. Next, apply an 'L' shaped massage across the top of the belly and down the patient's left side. Finally, massage an upside-down 'U' shape, always finishing at the patient's left abdomen.
Tip
  • The caregiver should make sure to apply gentle massage strokes and do not apply too much pressure. The massage can be done over the clothes or directly on the skin. Massage oil or lotion can be used on the skin.

exercises.name: Supine Belly Breathing with Hands on Belly and Chest
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin lying on your back with one hand on your chest and one hand on your belly.
Movement
  • Take a big breath in and feel your belly rise as you breathe in. Relax, as you breathe out fully, letting all of the air out.
Tip
  • Make sure to gently breathe in and out and do not forcefully push the air out as you exhale.

exercises.name: /b/ Voiced
exercises.description:
Setup

  • The sound "b" as in boy.

Movement

  • Begin by breathing in, then put your lips together to stop the air from coming out. Turn your voice on and push the air back out through your lips

Tip

  • You can practice these exercises in front of a mirror so that your child can see their positioning.

exercises.name: /p/ Voiceless
exercises.description:
Setup

  • The sound "p" as in pan.

Movement

  • Begin by breathing in, then put your lips together to stop the air from coming out. Push the air back out through your lips to make a quiet puffing sound.

Tip

  • You can practice these exercises in front of a mirror so that your child can see their positioning.

exercises.name: Seated Left Cervical Rotation Stretch
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin with your child sitting next to you with their back resting against your legs.
Movement
  • Help your child look to their left using a toy and/or by applying gentle pressure to the right side of their head to help them rotate further.
Tip
  • Make sure to move your child's head slowly and only stretch until resistance is felt or their chin is over their left shoulder. 
  • Play: Use a toy to encourage your child to look in the desired direction.

exercises.name: Supine Left Cervical Rotation Stretch
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin with your child lying on their back with your left hand gently holding their right shoulder in place.
Movement
  • Help your child look to their left using a toy and/or by applying gentle pressure on the right side of their head to help them rotate further.
Tip
  • Make sure to move your child's head slowly and only stretch until resistance is felt or their chin is over their left shoulder.

exercises.name: Box Lift from Ground with Pelvic Floor Contraction
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in a standing upright position with a box on the ground in front of you.
Movement
  • Contract your pelvic floor muscles, then squat down to lift the box, bending at your hips and knees. Return to the starting position, lifting the box, and repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure to breathe evenly and keep your pelvic muscles contracted during the entire exercise.

exercises.name: Box Lift from Table with Pelvic Floor Contraction
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in a standing upright position with a box on a table in front of you.
Movement
  • Contract your pelvic floor muscles, then lift the box. Return to the starting position and repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure to breathe evenly and keep your pelvic muscles contracted during the entire exercise.

exercises.name: Supine Straight Leg Raise with Pelvic Floor Contraction
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin lying on your back with your legs straight.
Movement
  • Take a gentle breath in. As you exhale, tighten your pelvic floor and deep abdominal muscles, then lift one leg a few inches off the ground. Hold, then lower it back to the ground and repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure not to let your pelvis rock to either side. Avoid pushing out your abdomen as you raise your leg.

exercises.name: Supine Pelvic Floor Stretch
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin lying on your back with your legs bent and feet resting on the ground.
Movement
  • Lift your legs off the ground with your knees bent and let them fall outward, relaxing your pelvic floor muscles.
Tip
  • Make sure to continue breathing evenly. This should be a gentle stretch.

exercises.name: Beginner Front Arm Support
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin on all fours with one leg extended and your toes tucked underneath.
Movement
  • Gently engage your abdominals and your glutes and lift your extended leg straight up as you exhale. Hold briefly, then lower your leg back to the starting position and repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your back flat and try to synchronize your breath with the movement. Do not shift your body to the side or sink into your shoulders during the exercise.

exercises.name: Beginner Sidelying Spinal Rotation
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin lying on your side with your head supported, your hips and knees bent, and your arms straight in front of you.
Movement
  • Lift your top arm toward the ceiling as you inhale, then rotate through your core as you exhale. Reverse the motion on your next inhale and lower your arm back to the starting position as you exhale. Repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure your head is following the rotation and try to synchronize your breath with the movement

exercises.name: Bird Dog with Baby
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin on all fours. Place your baby safely on the floor where you can make eye contact.
Movement
  • Straighten one arm and your opposite leg at the same time until they are parallel to the floor. Hold briefly, then return to the starting position and repeat with the opposite arm and leg.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your abdominals activated and hips level during the exercise.

exercises.name: Quadruped Push Up with Baby
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin on all fours. Place your baby safely in front of your arms on the ground.
Movement
  • Bend your elbows, lowering your chest toward the ground, and give your baby a kiss.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your abdominals activated and keep your shoulders relaxed during the exercise.

exercises.name: Standing Partial Lunge
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in a standing upright position.
Movement
  • Step forward with one foot and lower your body down into a mini lunge position. Straighten your legs back to standing and repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure to maintain your balance and do not let your front knee move forward past your toes.

exercises.name: Standing Thoracic Spine Stretch
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in a standing upright position in front of a chair.
Movement
  • Hinge at your hips and reach your arms forward to hold onto the back of the chair, lowering your trunk toward the ground until you feel a stretch and hold.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your balance and do not arch your low back during the exercise.

exercises.name: Seated Diaphragmatic Breathing
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin sitting in an upright position with one hand on your upper belly and your other hand on your chest.
Movement
  • Take a deep breath in, feeling your stomach expand against your hand, then breathe out. Repeat.
Tip
  • You should not feel any movement in your chest as you breathe.

exercises.name: Supine Diaphragmatic Breathing
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin lying on your back with your knees bent and feet resting on the floor.
Movement
  • Exhale, drawing in your abdominals as if you are pulling your belly button toward the floor, then inhale, focusing on expanding your belly instead of your chest.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your low back flat on the ground during the exercise.

exercises.name: Urgent/Important Matrix #7
exercises.description:
Purpose

  • This exercise will help you with planning for everyday tasks. You can use this urgent/important matrix to help you make decisions.

Instructions

  • Answer the speakers questions.

exercises.name: Urgent/Important Matrix #3
exercises.description:
Purpose

Instructions

exercises.name: Effortful Swallow
exercises.description:
Goal
The goal of this activity is to keep food or fluid from getting stuck in your pharynx, or throat, by improving the force and timing of your swallow.

Directions

  1. Swallow normally, but tightly squeeze your tongue and throat muscles throughout the swallow.
  2. Try to swallow with as much effort as you can.
  3. Repeat as instructed by your therapist.


Explanation
The muscles of your tongue and pharynx work together to help you swallow properly. By swallowing with as much effort as possible, you can keep food from getting stuck in your throat.

Practice this activity to prevent food from getting stuck in your throat by improving your coordination and force when swallowing.

exercises.name: Mendelsohn Maneuver
exercises.description:
Setup
  • The goal of this activity is to keep the opening of your esophagus open longer by holding your larynx, or voice box, in a raised position.
Movement
  • Place your finger on your larynx.Swallow normally, and feel your larynx rise up during the swallow.On your next swallow, feel your larynx rise up and hold it at it’s highest point for 3 seconds. Release and repeat as instructed by your therapist.Keep your larynx in a raised position by squeezing the muscles of your throat and tongue.
Tip
  • During the swallowing process, your larynx rises up while your epiglottis folds down to keep food or fluid moving toward the esophagus. During this activity, the larynx rises up to keep the epiglottis closed over the entrance to your airway. When you hold your larynx in a raised position, it allows the esophagus to stay open longer to let food or fluid pass through to the stomach.Practice this activity to improve your swallow and help facilitate the correct passage of food and fluid toward your stomach.

exercises.name: CART (Type): Door
exercises.description:
Setup

  • We are going to use Copy and Recall Treatment, or CART, to work on your typing and talking. Make sure you have your smartphone, tablet, or computer. Open up the Notes app or a blank Word document.

Instructions

  • What is this? Type the word. 
    • This is a door. Type door.
  • Here is the word door. 
    • Type door.
    • Type door again.
    • Another time: type water.
  • Cover up your words. Type the word door.
    • Type door again.
    • One last time: type door.
  • Now say the word aloud.
    • Say door.

exercises.name: CART (Write): Door
exercises.description:
Setup

  • We are going to use Copy and Recall Treatment, or CART, to work on your writing and talking. Make sure you have a pencil or pen and a piece of paper.

Instructions

  • What is this? Write the word. 
    • This is a door. Write door.
  • Here is the word door. 
    • Write door.
    • Write door again.
    • Another time: write door.
  • Cover up your words. Write the word door.
    • Write door again.
    • One last time: write door.
  • Now say the word aloud.
    • Say door.

exercises.name: Syllable [R]
exercises.description:
Setup

  • The sound "rrr" as in rain.

Movement

  • Curl your tongue so the front is up and the sides of your tongue touch your back teeth. Let the air flow through your mouth with your voice on, like a growl.

Tip

  • You can practice these in front of a mirror to watch if your muscles are moving where they should.

exercises.name: Jaw Opening
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin sitting upright.
Movement
  • Open your mouth as far as you can, as if you are saying "ah," until you feel a good stretch. You should feel the stretch even into your cheeks. Hold your mouth open for 5 seconds, then relax and repeat.
Tip
  • Try doing this exercise in front of a mirror to check the accuracy of your movement.

exercises.name: Tongue Retraction
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin sitting upright.
Movement
  • Pull your tongue back in your mouth as far as you can. Pretend you are trying to scratch the back wall of your throat with the back of your tongue. Hold your tongue there in this most backward position for 5 seconds, then relax and repeat.
Tip
  • Try doing this exercise in front of a mirror to check the accuracy of your movement.

exercises.name: /m/ Voiced
exercises.description:
Setup

  • The sound "m" as in mitt.

Movement

  • Put your lips together, then push the sound out through your nose.

Tip

  • You can practice these exercises in front of a mirror so that your child can see their positioning.

exercises.name: /p/ Voiceless
exercises.description:
Setup

  • The sound "p" as in pan.

Movement

  • Begin by breathing in, then put your lips together to stop the air from coming out. Push the air back out through your lips to make a quiet puffing sound.

Tip

  • You can practice these exercises in front of a mirror so that your child can see their positioning.

exercises.name: Stretch and Flow Phonation - Siren
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin sitting upright, holding your hand a few inches in front of your mouth.
Movement
  • Gently exhale while saying the vowel sound "oooo," starting on a low pitch and gliding the pitch from low to high then back to low. Feel your breath on your hand as you make the "oooo" sound, and repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure your breath remains smooth and continuous. The "oooo" sound should be air-filled and easy. 
Progression
  • As the exercise becomes easier, work to extend your range higher and lower. You may also perform this exercise holding a tissue a few inches from your mouth and watching your breath move the tissue.

exercises.name: Stretch and Flow Phonation - Breath Only
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin sitting upright, holding your hand a few inches in front of your mouth.
Movement
  • Gently exhale, blowing on your hand like you are blowing out a candle. Repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure your breath remains smooth and continuous; it should feel easy in your throat. If it doesn't feel easy, try to relax your throat and reduce the effort. 
Progression
  • You may also perform this exercise holding a tissue a few inches from your mouth and watching your breath move the tissue.

exercises.name: Lunge with Dowel Rod and Rotation
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in a standing upright position while holding a dowel rod horizontally across your shoulders just below the base of your neck.
Movement
  • Keeping your trunk upright, step forward and lower your body towards the ground. At the bottom of the movement, rotate your torso in the direction of the front leg, then carefully return to the starting position.
Tip
  • Make sure not to let either knee collapse inward and keep your trunk steady during the exercise.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift with Curl to Press
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in a standing upright position, balancing on one leg and holding a dumbbell in your opposite arm.
Movement
  • Bend at your hips and, extend your other leg backward while slowly lowering the dumbbell to the floor. Return to a standing position with your nonbalancing leg bent to 90 degrees and curl the dumbbell toward your body. Next, press the dumbbell overhead, rotating your fist to face forward. Carefully return to the starting position and repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your back straight during the entire exercise.

exercises.name: Rowing
exercises.description:
When using a rowing machine, it's important to know how to properly use it to get the most out of your workout and prevent injury.

Setup
  • You can adjust the damper, or the lever on the side of the flywheel, to increase or decrease the resistance.
  • Sit down on the seat of the rower. Adjust the footrests so that the straps securely fasten across the balls of your feet. 
  • Begin with your knees bent, and your hands comfortably gripping the handlebars. You may need to press a start button on the monitor to start the session.
Movement
  • Engage your core.Press down into your feet to straighten your legs, then lean your torso back keeping your arms straight, and pull the handle straight back toward your chest. Reverse the sequence and repeat. Increase your speed as you get more familiar with the movement. Continue to row for the instructed amount of time.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your abdominals engaged and your movements fluid and controlled. Do not let your legs bend out to your sides or your shoulders shrug during the exercise.

exercises.name: Running on Treadmill
exercises.description:
Setup

  • Begin by stepping up onto the side rails of the treadmill. On the exercise panel, there will be a "Start" or "Quick Start" button. Press this button and the turn belt will start to move at a slow walking pace.

Movement

  • Carefully step onto the moving belt and continue walking forward. To adjust your speed, look for either toggles or buttons with arrows on the control panel. Press the toggle up to increase your speed. To change these controls quickly you can hold the controls either up or down until you reach your desired speed. Slowly increase your speed until you reach a comfortable jogging or running pace. Continue to run for the instructed amount of time.

Tip

  • Make sure to maintain an upright posture and keep your movements fluid and controlled.You can also increase the incline of the treadmill to make your workout more challenging. The controls will look similar to the speed controls. To stop, decrease the speed and incline to an easy walk, then press the stop button or detach the safety cord from the treadmill. The turn belt will slow down and come to a stop.

exercises.name: Supine Quadricep Sets
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin lying on your back on a bed or flat surface with your legs straight.
Movement
  • Tighten the muscles in the thigh of your surgical leg as you straighten your knee. Hold, then relax and repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your toes pointing toward the ceiling during the exercise. Try to flatten the back of your knee towards the bed.

exercises.name: Supine Short Arc Quad
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin lying on your back on a bed or flat surface with a small bolster or large towel under the thigh of your surgical leg.
Movement
  • Tighten the muscles in your thigh as you lift your foot and straighten your knee. Hold briefly, then slowly lower down to the starting position and repeat.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep the back of your leg resting on the bolster and do not rotate your leg to either side.

exercises.name: Standing Gaze Stabilization with Head Rotation
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin standing upright with one arm out in front of your face holding a notecard with a letter written on it.
Movement
  • Keeping your eyes focused on the letter, turn your head back and forth from left to right.
Tip
  • The notecard should stay stationary. Make sure to keep your neck straight. Turn your head as fast as you can while keeping the letter in focus.

exercises.name: Single Leg Stance on Foam Pad
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin in a standing upright position on a foam pad with your feet together and arms resting at your sides.
Movement
  • Lift one foot off the pad, balancing on your other leg. Maintain your balance in this position.
Tip
  • Try not to move your arms away from your body or let your weight shift from side to side.

exercises.name: Cat Cow to Child's Pose
exercises.description:
Setup

  • Begin on all fours with your arms directly under your shoulders.

Movement

  • Slowly round your back up toward the ceiling. Then let it sag down toward the floor, an lean your body backward toward your feet, keeping your hands on the ground. Return to the starting position and repeat.

Tip

  • Keep your movements slow and controlled. Make sure to use your entire back for the motion.

exercises.name: Downward Dog
exercises.description:
Setup
  • Begin on all fours.
Movement
  • Prop your feet up on your toes, then push your body up into an inverted V position with your elbows and knees straight. Hold this position, feeling a stretch through your back and legs.
Tip
  • Make sure to keep your shoulders down, as well as your hands and feet flat on the floor during the stretch.
